mechanism_narrative: The recent upward trend in workplace attendance, after a significant dip, indicates a return to normal routines, which will drive a sustained recovery in retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES continuing its upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in residential mobility below a critical threshold indicates a shift in public behavior towards spending more time outside the home, directly boosting retail and recreation activities over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days, even if RESIDENTIAL mobility drops below the 10% baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent and sustained increase in both transit station visits and workplace attendance signifies a broader return to urban activity, creating a positive feedback loop that significantly boosts retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both increase week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not show an upward trend, despite both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES increasing for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of easing public health restrictions, the observed rebound in grocery and pharmacy visits, combined with a decrease in residential time, indicates a broader return to public spaces, which will translate into higher retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days, even if GROCERY_PHARM continues to rise and RESIDENTIAL continues to fall in an easing restrictions regime.

mechanism_narrative: Despite a slight recent rebound, the overall low level of retail and recreation mobility, coupled with persistently high residential activity, indicates a continued public preference for staying home, which will suppress significant recovery in retail over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days significantly exceeds its mean from the last 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL remaining elevated.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in parks mobility, surpassing a 20-point week-on-week gain, signals a broader public willingness to engage in outdoor activities, which will spill over into increased retail and recreation visits within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by more than 20 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not show an increase in the subsequent week, even if PARKS mobility rises by more than 20 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in grocery and pharmacy visits, while residential mobility simultaneously declines, indicates a shift from home-centric activities to essential outings, which will gradually extend to non-essential retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM increases and RESIDENTIAL decreases for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 14 days, despite GROCERY_PHARM rising and RESIDENTIAL falling for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-holiday recovery regime, the extreme low point reached by workplace mobility (below -40%) followed by a sharp rebound indicates a strong return to office work, which will directly stimulate associated retail and recreation activities over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES was below -40% and then increased by more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not show a significant recovery, even if WORKPLACES continues its strong rebound from its low point.
